question: Should the fix intentionally invalidate all four affected cost-cache artifacts on upgrade to recover offsets that may have advanced past incomplete tails?
rationale: The invalidation is technically consistent with the fix but can trigger expensive rescans for existing users, so the upgrade tradeoff requires ownership confirmation.

options.title: Accept one-time rebuild
options.body: Keep the version bumps because existing cache files cannot reveal whether their stored offsets passed an incomplete tail.

options.title: Narrow the rebuild scope
options.body: Limit invalidation only if maintainers can prove some providers or cache families never persist offsets produced by this scanner.

options.title: Pause pending migration design
options.body: Defer the PR and design a compatible cache migration if full-history rescans are unacceptable for large installations.

recommendation.title: Accept one-time rebuild
recommendation.body: Keep the version bumps because existing cache files cannot reveal whether their stored offsets passed an incomplete tail.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest observed history on the JSONL chunk-scanner implementation affected by the offset semantics.
